pyqs.independentSolution: Starting from rest, each gains eV. Nonrelativistically p²=2mK=2meV, so λ=h/√(2meV). Dividing electron by proton expression yields √(mp/me). Both charges have magnitude e; acceleration uses opposite directions of electric force. Zero voltage is excluded; equal speed would instead give mp/me.

Define e>0 as charge magnitude: q=−e, field −2E₀ along x, force +2eE₀ along x. v=v₀+2eE₀t/m, p=mv, λ=h/(mv). Since λ₀=h/(4mv₀), λ(0)=4λ₀. Wavelength decreases for t≥0; nonrelativistic regime explicitly stated.

targetQuestionText: An electron and a proton start from rest and are each accelerated through the same positive potential difference V. Their masses are mₑ and mₚ. In the nonrelativistic regime, what is the ratio λₑ/λₚ of their de Broglie wavelengths?
